gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Megrim cuts stencil-like, angular letters of one steady width, giving every line a futuristic, measured edge. Noto Sans Kannada handles the friendly part, with s curves opening wide.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-kayah-li: Angular and futuristic, Megrim is drawn like rounded rod in a single weight, while Noto Sans Kayah Li lifts its brush ends. Give the body text a touch more size.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-kharoshthi: Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a dark, dense stripe of lowercase, its curves never quite closing back on themselves. Megrim brings angular, futuristic punch, its strokes carrying no shading at all.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer stands tall and open, its small letters nearly capital-sized, with generous notches in every curve. Megrim, bent from a single length of wire, likes plenty of size.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Sharp and spare: Megrim's s holds spine and terminals to one thickness, while Noto Sans Khojki leaves wide exits. Over a full paragraph, Khojki's big e eyes keep the text light.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Noto Sans Khudawadi reads with little height contrast between capitals and lowercase, its rounds left unlatched like a hook. Megrim's t has a crossbar matching its stem, angular and futuristic.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-kr: A skyward x-height line gives Megrim its angular, futuristic look, with diagonals drawn to match its stems. And Noto Sans KR does the plain work, with stubby ascenders and generous curve gaps.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-lao: Sharp and skyward: Megrim holds every stroke to a constant thickness, angular and futuristic. And Noto Sans Lao, its x-height pushed high and mouths open, would carry page after page smoothly.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Megrim's strokes hold their thickness from end to end, giving angular, futuristic letters a measured, wiry look. Noto Sans Lao Looped forms solid word blocks, so a modest size should suit it.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu reads tall and gaping, its curves stretched wide. Megrim does the angular, futuristic showpiece, its thin joins no thinner than its stems, while Limbu does the friendly everyday work.
